intro: Each setting is saved as soon as you change it, in the club database, so it follows its backups. Only the AI keys stay on this computer, outside the database.

season.title: Season
season.help: This month applies to statistics, the annual report and the Rowers and Boats pages in Management.
season.changed: Reports and the dashboard now use the season from {{start}} to {{end}}.
season.description: The dates that bound a season in the statistics.

rankings.title: Rankings
rankings.public: Show rankings with rowers' names at the boathouse, without the admin password
rankings.help: Applies to: {{reports}}. Turn on only if members agree to appear in rankings shown at the boathouse.
rankings.description: What the boathouse screen shows without a password.
rankings.publicWarning: Everyone at the boathouse sees these rankings with names. Check that members were told (GDPR).

ai.title: Built-in AI assistant

status.keychain: Key saved in this computer's keychain: never in the club database, its backups or its exports.
status.file: Key saved in a protected file on this computer: never in the club database, its backups or its exports.
status.error: Could not read the key status. Try again; if the problem continues, save the key again.
status.noServer: No server saved on this computer.
status.serverWithKey: Server saved on this computer: {{url}}, with a key.
status.serverWithoutKey: Server saved on this computer: {{url}}, without a key.
status.keychainHint: Key …{{hint}} saved in this computer's keychain: never in the club database, its backups or its exports.
status.fileHint: Key …{{hint}} saved in a protected file on this computer: never in the club database, its backups or its exports.
status.serverWithKeyHint: Server saved on this computer: {{url}}, with key …{{hint}}.

keyPlaceholder.openai_compatible: Empty for a server without a key

ai.deleteConfirm: The {{provider}} key will be erased from this computer. Without another key, the assistant switches to copy-paste mode.

invalidFormat.openai_compatible: The key must be 8 to 1,000 characters, without spaces.
invalidFormat.anthropicKey: This is an Anthropic key: choose the Anthropic provider to use it.

ai.shareAssetsHelp: Lets you ask for "outings of the Albatross". Rowers' names are never sent.

createKey.anthropic: Create a key on <site>console.anthropic.com</site>, then paste it here.
createKey.openai: Create a key on <site>platform.openai.com</site>, then paste it here.

ai.noKeyHint: Without a key, the assistant still works: it prepares a request to copy into your AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Le Chat…), then you paste its answer.
ai.whatIsSent: What is sent to {{provider}}: your question, the structure of the statistics tables, the club's outing types and today's date. Never rowers' names, outings or results.

sent.question: your question, exactly as you write it (hence the advice not to put names in it);
sent.schema: the structure of the statistics tables: column names and descriptions, never their content;
sent.context: the club's outing types, the enabled modules, the season start and today's date;
sent.assets: boat and route names, only when the option above is on;
sent.errors: after an error, the query's error message, so that the AI can fix it.

never.people: rowers' names, birth dates, contact details and notes;
never.outings: outings, comments and calculation results: the query runs on this computer and its results stay there;
never.password: the admin password and the rest of the club database.

privacy.copyPaste: Without a key, you paste the same request into your AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT…) yourself: it contains exactly these items.

where.anthropic: The request goes straight from this computer to api.anthropic.com, through no other server.
where.openai: The request goes straight from this computer to api.openai.com, through no other server. The app asks OpenAI not to keep the answer ("store" turned off).
where.serverLocal: The server {{host}} runs on this computer: the request does not leave it.
where.serverRemote: The request goes from this computer to {{host}}. What that server does with it is up to it: read its terms of use.
where.serverUnknown: The request goes to the server address you save, and to no other.

privacy.title: Privacy

provider.label: AI provider
provider.help: Each provider keeps its own key on this computer: switching does not delete any key.
provider.anthropicHelp: An API key created on console.anthropic.com, with prepaid credit (a Claude Pro subscription is not enough).
provider.openaiHelp: An API key created on platform.openai.com, with prepaid credit (a ChatGPT subscription is not enough).
provider.openai_compatibleHelp: A service that follows OpenAI's format: Mistral, OpenRouter, or a model installed on this computer (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp…).
provider.mismatch: The built-in assistant uses the provider chosen here. {{provider}} has no key yet: until then, the assistant works in copy-paste mode.

ai.costPerQuestion: About {{cost}} per typical question, billed to the club's {{provider}} account (estimate).

compatibleModel.label: Model name
compatibleModel.help: As the server names it, for example "mistral-large-latest" or "llama3.3".
compatibleModel.required: Enter the model name to check the server and ask questions.

baseUrl.label: Server address
baseUrl.help: The API's base address, often ending in /v1. Over https, except for a server on this computer.
baseUrl.local: Server on this computer: the table structure and your questions do not leave it.
baseUrl.remote: {{host}} is not on this computer. It will receive the table structure and your questions, as Anthropic or OpenAI would. Choose a service you trust.
baseUrl.changed: New address: also enter its key if it needs one. A saved key is never sent to another address.

invalid.invalid: Address not recognised: it should look like https://example.org/v1.
invalid.insecure: A server that is not on this computer must use https://, so that the key is not sent in clear text.
invalid.credentials: The address must not contain a user name or password: put the key in its own field.
invalid.query: The address must not contain "?" or "#".

ai.billedServer: Any cost depends on the server: a server on this computer costs nothing.
ai.deleteConfirmServer: The server and its key will be erased from this computer. Without another key, the assistant switches to copy-paste mode.
ai.description: Used by "Ask the AI" in the Explorer.
ai.savedCheckFailed: Key saved, but the check failed: {{error}}
ai.savedCheckFailedServer: Server saved, but the check failed: {{error}}

mcp.title: Your AI app (MCP)
mcp.enabled: Let the AI apps on this computer read the club's statistics
mcp.help: Ask questions about the club's statistics right in Claude Desktop, the ChatGPT app (Codex), Cursor or VS Code. They read this computer's database, read-only, and can propose charts, which you accept in Explorer › Proposals.
mcp.whatIsSent: Unlike the built-in assistant, your app reads the results (the figures) and sends them to its provider to answer you: Anthropic for Claude, OpenAI for ChatGPT and Codex, the one chosen in Cursor or VS Code.

pseudonymised.title: Codes instead of names (recommended)
pseudonymised.description: Rowers appear as a code (R-1A2B3C4D): no name, birth date, contact details or comments.

nominative.title: Rowers' names visible
nominative.description: Your app sees the names; they go to its provider with the results.

mcp.nominativeWarning: Your app's answers go through its provider (Anthropic, OpenAI…): rowers' names will leave this computer. Check that this matches what members were told (GDPR).
mcp.linux: Claude Desktop does not exist on Linux: choose another app above (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code…).
mcp.copyFailed: Could not copy: select the text and copy it.
mcp.appImage: AppImage version: the path changes if you move the file. Copy the configuration again after moving or updating it.
mcp.macosTemporary: Rowing Beacon runs from a temporary location (disk image or Downloads folder). Drag the app into the Applications folder, open it again, then copy the configuration: otherwise your AI app will no longer find it.
mcp.disabledNote: Off: no app can read the statistics. An app already set up gets a message saying access is closed.
mcp.infoError: Could not prepare the AI app configuration. Try again; if the problem continues, restart the application.
mcp.clientsHelp: Choose your app: each has its own configuration.
mcp.otherClients: Another MCP-compatible app? Give it this command (local "stdio" server):
mcp.lastCallNone: No app has connected on this computer yet: follow the steps below.
mcp.clientsNote: Changing these settings does not require copying the configuration again.

steps.pasteMcpServers: Paste the configuration. If the file already contains "mcpServers", only add the "rowing-beacon" entry.
steps.ask: Restart {{app}}, then ask it for example: "How many outings did the club do this season?"
steps.claudeDesktopOpen: In Claude Desktop, open Settings › Developer › Edit Config: the claude_desktop_config.json file opens ({{path}}).
steps.claudeCodeRun: Paste it in a terminal and press Enter. Claude Code can then read the statistics from any folder on this computer.
steps.claudeCodeAsk: Open Claude Code, then ask it for example: "How many outings did the club do this season?"
steps.codexOpen: Open the file {{path}} (create it if it does not exist). The ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the Codex extension share this file.
steps.codexPaste: Add the configuration at the end of the file, then save it.
steps.cursorOpen: Open the file {{path}} (create it if it does not exist).
steps.vscodeOpen: In VS Code, open the Command Palette and run "MCP: Open User Configuration".
steps.vscodePaste: Paste the configuration. If the file already contains "servers", only add the "rowing-beacon" entry.
steps.vscodeAsk: Restart VS Code, then ask Copilot in Agent mode, for example: "How many outings did the club do this season?"
